parent: HR Healthcare Ltd t/a Treated (company 06790962, Bolton); footer also names Webcare Group Limited; pharmacy GPhC 9010946
model: Multi-condition UK online doctor and pharmacy; hair loss is a men-only condition sold through one generic questionnaire with licensed and off-label tablets and branded minoxidil on monthly-to-6-monthly subscriptions.

access.accountWall: Checkout 'Patient details' page (start.treated.com/GBR/en/#/checkout): first name, last name, date of birth, email, phone. Reached after the questionnaire, height/weight, medical profile, the treatment options screen and the product questions. The full recommendation screen and prices are shown before the wall.
blockers: Women cannot start the hair-loss consultation (sex gate hard stop).
Occasional late cookie banner and timing flakes in replays (one Regaine walk failed twice).
access.coverageNote: Men's flow walked to the treatment options screen in 21 one-change replays (runs/e00–e20) plus stage 1 walks to the account wall from the general entry and the Dutasteride, Avodart, Regaine and Propecia entries. Question set and per-option actions from the served definition (quiz-definition-male.json); product list, prices and automatic-offer limits from gettreatmentoptions, compared run by run (scripts/summ.js, scripts/odiff.js). Women: hard stop. Nothing after the account wall. Stage 3 (verify) replayed both baselines and 11 more cases fresh (runs/verify-*), re-read the live product pages and found the review/auto messages are only in the server response, not on screen.

products.name: Finasteride 1mg tablets (generic)
products.legalStatus: POM, licensed for male pattern hair loss
products.priceDetail: 56 tablets every 2 months £55.95; 84 every 3 months £73.95; 168 every 6 months £130.95. Free delivery. Cancellable auto-renewing subscription.
products.recommendedWhen: Default for every man who reaches the options screen from the general entry, in both automatic and review mode (all observed runs). Automatic-offer limits: age 18–49, BMI 35 or under, nothing in the medical profile except smoking or drinking. Removed only by the mental-illness hard stop.

products.name: Propecia 1mg tablets (branded finasteride)
products.legalStatus: POM, licensed for male pattern hair loss
products.priceDetail: 56 every 2 months £114.95; 84 every 3 months £149.95; 168 every 6 months £287.95.
products.recommendedWhen: Always listed (rank 3) for men who pass the hard stops; pre-selected only from the Propecia product link (runs/e15-propecia-save). Same limits as generic finasteride.

products.name: Dutasteride 0.5mg capsules (generic)
products.legalStatus: POM, licensed for enlarged prostate; prescribed off-label for hair loss (the site says so)
products.recommendedWhen: Listed for every review-mode case. In the automatic offer only for men who neither smoke (including ex-smokers) nor drink alcohol (runs/e16, e17, e19). Pre-selected only from its product link, and then only if it passes those limits (runs/e20). Never the default from the general entry, even after finasteride use.

products.name: Avodart 0.5mg capsules (branded dutasteride)
products.legalStatus: POM, licensed for enlarged prostate; off-label for hair loss
products.priceDetail: 60 every 2 months £81.95; 90 every 3 months £113.95 (the 90 pack is marked most popular).
products.recommendedWhen: Same as Dutasteride: listed in review mode; in the automatic offer only for non-smoking, non-drinking men; pre-selected only from its product link.

products.name: Regaine for Men Extra Strength 5% (scalp solution 3x60ml or foam 3x73ml)
products.form: topical solution or foam, twice daily
products.legalStatus: Licensed non-prescription medicine (site: 'available over the counter'; P or GSL class not checked)
products.priceDetail: 3x73ml (foam, half a capful twice daily) £104.95 every 3 months. Only one plan length each. The options data carries an old 'Starting from £55.95' tag; the live price shown is £99.95.
products.recommendedWhen: Always listed (rank 2) for men who pass the hard stops, including men with low blood pressure or heart disease (heart sends the case to review but does not remove it). Pre-selected only from its product link. Same limits as finasteride; no product questions.

products.name: Finasteride + Minoxidil Drops (custom made)
products.legalStatus: Unlicensed combined formulation made to order (the page says 'currently unlicensed')
products.priceDetail: Product page and category page both show 'Not available' on 2026-11-23; it is not in the consultation's options list.
products.recommendedWhen: Never offered: the page says "Not available" and the product is absent from every treatment-options response (all runs).

flows.name: Hair loss consultation (men only)
flows.stagesSummary: Start page → sex (+18+/terms) → 11 hair-loss questions → GP info → height/weight → medical profile (9 ticks) → confirm → 'checking what's safe' → treatment options (pre-selected product, Edit, Choose for me) → product questions (1 for finasteride, 3 for dutasteride/Avodart, none for Regaine) → checkout patient details = account wall. Product buttons (…&product=024-143 Finasteride, 024-313 Propecia, 024-1973 Dutasteride, 024-1915 Avodart, 024-322 Regaine, &uf=prod) use the same questions and only change the pre-selected product.

In Auto mode products that fail their own limits are hidden from the Edit list (smoking or alcohol hides both dutasteride products) and the default falls back to Finasteride; in Offline mode all five are listed. The product link pre-selects that product when it is allowed.

engineSummary: Treated runs one short men-only questionnaire (11 questions, height and weight, a general medical profile) and then always shows the same five products with prices, with Finasteride 1mg pre-selected (or the product of the page the man came from). The answers do not choose the medicine. They decide two things: whether the man is stopped (female, or any history of mental illness), and whether the case is an automatic offer or goes to clinician review. That decision sits in the server response (mode Auto or Offline); the patient sees the same screen either way. Almost any non-standard answer, and simply never having used treatment or not having seen a doctor, sends the case to review, so most first-time buyers are reviewed after paying. Only in the automatic offer are per-product limits applied: smoking or any alcohol removes the two dutasteride products. Date of birth is asked only after the account wall. BMI over 35 sends the whole case to review, even from the Dutasteride link.
strengths: Full price list, all strengths and plans, and a pre-selected product shown before any contact details: very low friction.
Fast, clear questionnaire (11 short questions plus height, weight and a profile) with tick-box answers.
Server-side automatic-offer engine with per-product limits (age, BMI, smoking, drinking, medical profile), so products can be filtered without changing the questions.
Clear safety stop for a history of mental illness with finasteride, and explicit off-label and side-effect acknowledgements for dutasteride before checkout.
Product landing pages pre-select their product, so ad traffic lands straight on what it clicked.
weaknesses: No women's hair-loss service (hard stop on sex). The only women's products (Regaine for Women) sit in a telogen effluvium category marked "Not available".
The answers barely personalise the offer: the same five products and the same default for almost everyone; previous treatment, failure or side effects do not move a man to a different product.
The mental-illness stop is blunt: it blocks minoxidil too, and anxiety alone ends the consultation.
Low blood pressure is not screened against minoxidil; heart disease only flags review and Regaine stays listed.
Age is not asked until checkout, so the 18–49 limit cannot act before the wall.

Blanket review flags (never used treatment, not seen a doctor) mean most first-time buyers go to clinician review; the screen does not tell them so (the review message is only in the server response).
Smoking (even ex-smokers) or any alcohol removes dutasteride from the automatic offer; we could not see a clinical reason for this (our judgement, not the company's statement).
No scalp photos, no Norwood stage, no goals or preferences (tablet vs topical) asked before the wall.
Compounded finasteride + minoxidil drops listed but not available; no topical finasteride, no oral minoxidil, no combination spray.

verification.verdict: Trustworthy as labelled for what an anonymous man sees. Both baselines and the eight highest-impact rules (female stop, mental-illness stop, smoking and alcohol removing dutasteride, product-link fallback, BMI, low blood pressure, review flags) were re-tested live and held. The one real error was presentational: earlier stages said the review or recommendation message appears on screen, but it only exists in the server response, so a patient cannot tell an automatic offer from a review case. Prices and strengths match the live pages. Remaining gaps are code-based rules marked as code, the age limit and everything behind the account wall.
